votes.why: the repeated low-detail creature models scattered across the lava field.

the repeating, flat-looking procedural textures on the lava floor and foreground rock, along with simple creature models, make it look like a competent but ordinary CG render rather than film-grade work.
the flat unshaded ground plane and lack of cast shadows or lava bounce light on the creatures
the cliff walls break into large angular slabs covered with the same stretched rock texture.

a fantastical lava-field scene with spindly creatures, good atmospheric depth and glowing lava cracks, reads like film or game concept art or a cinematic. Some repeated, smeared textures and the soft creature detail keep it from being certain, so c is the main alternative.
the lava crust's repetitive, procedurally patterned ridges
the visibly stretched, swirly procedural noise texture on the lava ground (typical hobbyist Blender render artifact)

the visibly stretched procedural terrain displacement and simple wave-pattern lava shader paired with shallow depth of field look like an ordinary offline 3D render rather than a top-budget film or real-time mobile/web demo.

the ground and lava-bank textures are swirly procedural patterns with visible stretching and repetition, which reads as an ordinary or hobbyist 3D render, not top-budget work. The atmosphere and depth of field are good enough that d is the close second.

procedural-looking lava terrain and repeated creature models with generic DOF, reads as a hobbyist/stock CG render rather than film-grade or real.

the detailed lava-rock textures, depth of field, atmospheric smoke and lighting look like high-end cinematic CG, though the odd creature forms and slightly soft detail leave some chance it's (c).

the creatures have detailed textures and strong atmospheric depth of field with volumetric haze and lava glow, which looks like a cinematic or concept-art render rather than a photo, and the slightly odd creature anatomy keeps it from clearly being (c).
the lava's uniform glowing crack pattern follows a visibly faceted mesh.
procedural-looking lava crack texture and simple spider-like creature models typical of a hobbyist Blender-style render.
the procedural Voronoi-like glowing lava veins paired with soft matte lighting and faceted cave-arch geometry typical of a standard 3D render.
the lava breaks into flat orange ribbons with sharp polygonal edges.

The rock detail, the dust haze and the cinematic composition with tiny spider creatures for scale look like film-quality CG. The lava is a bit procedural and graphic, and the flat foreground water is simple, so (c) is a close second.
